samples.question: The picture shows a track of nine grey square cells in a row. Number the cells 1 to 9 from left to right. Two discs stand on the track, one red and one blue, in two different cells: a disc is in the cell whose centre is nearest to the centre of that disc. Below the track is a row of cream cards, applied one at a time in order from left to right, as the grey arrow under the row shows. Each card carries one coloured spot, one green arrow and one or two purple dots. The coloured spot says which disc that card moves, the red disc or the blue disc. The green arrow says which way that disc moves, left or right: the arrow points the way the disc moves. The number of purple dots says how many single-cell steps the card asks for. The steps of a card are taken one at a time. In a step the named disc moves one cell in the card's direction; if the other disc is already standing in the cell the named disc is moving into, the other disc is pushed one further cell in the same direction and the named disc takes its place. A step is refused if it would carry the named disc off the end of the track, or if it would push the other disc off the end of the track: on a refused step nothing moves, the rest of that card is lost, and the next card is then applied from wherever the discs stand. Discs never jump over one another and never share a cell. The track is drawn only once, in the starting layout; no later position of either disc is drawn anywhere. After every card has been applied in order, which cell does the red disc end in? Answer with a single number from 1 to 9, counting cells from the left.
